title: Sophisticated computation, or primes, are not signs of intelligence

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Sophisticated computation, or primes, are not signs of intelligence

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Producing a signal by sophisticated computation is no evidence of intelligence, because such computation is common in ordinary physical processes; for instance, turbulence in the gas around a star quickly does more computation than all of human intellectual history, and sequences such as the primes can be generated by many non-intelligent systems.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. 12: The Principle of Computational Equivalence

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: And indeed it seems likely that for example an ordinary physical process like fluid turbulence in the gas around a star should rather quickly do more computation than has by most measures ever been done throughout the whole course of human intellectual history.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 12, “The Principle of Computational Equivalence”; section “Intelligence in the Universe” (from p. 822), p. 837. Scope: criteria for detecting extraterrestrial intelligence; natural physical processes

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch12-51: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.30

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Physical and computational data could support selected operation-count estimates, but the stated comparison has no invariant measurement. The conclusion about evidence of intelligence is epistemic and cannot be decided solely by observing sophisticated computation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: One could define a physical computation metric and estimate it for stellar turbulence, human computing, and prime-generating processes, but no standard metric makes these unlike systems commensurable or turns computational quantity into evidence about intelligence.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
There is no agreed measure of computation performed by a physical process.

Whether an observation counts as evidence of intelligence depends on priors and context.

The human-history comparison changes radically with the cost model.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A short program, and the recorded prime sequence, show that primes are produced by systems with no claim to intelligence, so that half is resolvable by computation. The stellar-turbulence comparison is quantitative and physical. Public turbulence databases support order-of-magnitude estimates for earthly flows, and they do not settle an accounting of computation around a star against human intellectual history.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fix a measure of computation and compare a model of turbulence in stellar gas with an estimate for recorded human calculation, and separately exhibit non-designed systems that output the primes. The primes half is immediate; the turbulence comparison is only approximated by existing flow databases.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Amount of computation is left as most measures, and those measures disagree.

A short prime generator settles only the easier half of the claim.

Laboratory turbulence is a proxy for gas around a star, and human intellectual history is not a standard dataset.
